results.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise
results.content:
## Introducing Firefox Enterprise

Firefox Enterprise is built for organizations with strict security, governance, and compliance requirements. It pairs the Firefox browser, built on Mozilla’s independent Gecko engine, with a management console organizations can run on their own infrastructure. From that console, IT teams can centrally manage browser policy and access, govern how data moves through the browser and set controls around AI use.

IT and security teams get more control over their data, IT infrastructure and browser environment — helping strengthen technological independence and operational resilience. [...] That means putting institutions in real control of the infrastructure and data they depend on, without asking them to rebuild or start over. Closing blind spots. Defining where policies, access and data live. Keeping core management within the institution’s environment. And bringing an overlooked layer — the browser — under institutional control.

Firefox Enterprise is unveiling across Europe with an initial sales focus on France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland, with more markets to follow. Thunderbird Enterprise is also in development, extending this customer-controlled approach to email and communications. We’ll have more to share as that work progresses.

If your organization wants greater control over its browser infrastructure, we’d like to work with you. [...] “If all your options are built with the same technology underneath, ‘choice’ is a lie. So is control,” said Anthony Enzor-DeMeo, CEO of Mozilla. “We built Firefox differently. And we’re bringing its independent architecture to institutions that are ready to rethink their dependencies and risk.”

## Bringing the browser under control

We’re starting with the browser because we see it as a key, but under-governed, layer. Firefox Enterprise gives institutions more control over the browser and the infrastructure managing it.

And because Firefox runs on Gecko, the only major browser engine developed outside Google and Apple, institutions have another path towards reducing dependence on a single architecture.

results.title: Mozilla Firefox Enterprise Gives Businesses More Control
results.content:
Mozilla has introduced Firefox Enterprise, a new browser designed for businesses and public bodies. The paid platform enables enterprises to meet strict regulatory and security requirements. With Mozilla’s Firefox Enterprise, businesses can control how sensitive data gets shared, manage employee access to web applications, and monitor device security.

## How Does the Firefox Enterprise Browser Work? [...] ## How Does the Firefox Enterprise Browser Work?

Mozilla’s enterprise platform combines the Firefox browser with a management dashboard hosted on the company’s own infrastructure. Mozilla, which added Perplexity AI to Firefox last year, said the new platform strengthens operational resilience. It gives IT and security teams expanded control over their browser environment, IT infrastructure, and data.

The Firefox browser management console allows IT  teams to set access rules, restrict AI tools, and link browser activity to current security monitoring systems. Additionally, teams can assign permissions and control where data goes. [...] Firefox uses the Gecko browser engine to render websites. Mozilla argues that using different browser engines can reduce shared exposure to vulnerabilities across an organization’s browsers.

“If all your options are built with the same technology underneath, ‘choice’ is a lie. So is control. We built Firefox differently. And we’re bringing its independent architecture to institutions that are ready to rethink their dependencies and risk,” Mozilla CEO Anthony Enzor-DeMeo said in a company statement. 

Initially, Mozilla will target businesses in France, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, with plans to expand into other markets. The company said organizations in these countries can request a demonstration, which includes standard professional support.

## Mozilla’s Firefox Enterprise combines an independent browser engine with a self-hostable management console, giving IT teams control over data, security policies, and AI access.

Firefox Mozilla

Credit: JHVEPhoto / Shutterstock

There’s growing talk of digital sovereignty as enterprises rethink past consolidation decisions made in the name of simplicity.

Mozilla, developer of Firefox, argues that a “very specific, very important layer” has been mostly missing from that conversation: The browser.

To that end, the company has unveiled Firefox Enterprise in a bid to diversify the browser engine to support privacy, control, and security.
